problem.original_text:
Let $$f(x)=x^5-5x+1$$.  
(a) Use calculus to determine the number of real roots of $$f(x)=0$$ by analyzing critical points and sign changes.  
(b) Approximate all real roots to 4 decimal places using Newton’s method starting from suitable initial guesses.  
(c) Include a plot of $$f(x)$$ on $$[-3,3]$$ showing roots and critical points.
problem.normalized_text:
Let $$f(x)=x^5-5x+1$$.  
(a) Use calculus to determine the number of real roots of $$f(x)=0$$ by analyzing critical points and sign changes.  
(b) Approximate all real roots to 4 decimal places using Newton’s method starting from suitable initial guesses.  
(c) Include a plot of $$f(x)$$ on $$[-3,3]$$ showing roots and critical points.

steps.title: Compute derivative and critical points
steps.explanation: f'(x)=5x^4-5 =5(x^4-1). Critical points where f'=0 are x=±1. f' positive for |x|>1, negative for |x|<1.

steps.title: Classify critical points
steps.explanation: Using sign of f': at x=-1 slope changes from + to - so local max; at x=1 slope changes from - to + so local min.
math_latex: $\text{So }x=-1\text{ is local max, }x=1\text{ is local min}$

steps.title: Evaluate f at critical points and ends
steps.explanation: Compute f(-1), f(1), and limits as x→±∞ to check sign changes for roots.

steps.title: Determine number of real roots
steps.explanation: Sign changes: from -∞ to f(-1)=5 gives one root left of -1; between -1 and 1 f changes 5→-3 gives another root; from f(1)=-3 to +∞ gives a third root. So three real roots.

steps.title: Choose Newton initial guesses
steps.explanation: Pick one initial guess in each sign-change interval: x0=-2, x0=0, x0=2 for left, middle, right roots respectively.

steps.title: Newton iteration formula
steps.explanation: Use Newton: x_{n+1}=x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n) with f and f' as above until 1e-8 tolerance to ensure 4 decimal digits.

steps.title: Perform iterations and report roots
steps.explanation: Iterations converged to three real roots; report approximations to 4 decimals.
